jane-austen.name: Jane Austen
jane-austen.caution: Close third person throughout, built on free indirect discourse. The cleanest single-voice, single-genre corpus in the collection — a strong romance and courtship-comedy contrast lens.

charlotte-bronte.name: Charlotte Bronte
charlotte-bronte.caution: Both novels are first-person retrospective narration (Jane Eyre; Lucy Snowe in Villette) in an intense, morally serious, gothic-tinged register. A coherent single-voice corpus and a strong romance / gothic-romance lens.

louisa-may-alcott.name: Louisa May Alcott
louisa-may-alcott.caution: Warm third-person domestic fiction of family and moral growth — a wholesome, found-family register close to cozy and women's fiction. Little Men moves to an ensemble school setting, which widens the cast and dialogue lanes.

elizabeth-gaskell.name: Elizabeth Gaskell
elizabeth-gaskell.caution: Cozy core only (the industrial novels North and South / Mary Barton are deliberately excluded). *Cranford* is a first-person episodic sketch-novel; *Cousin Phillis* and *Wives and Daughters* are third person, so whole-author POV numbers average across two lanes.

kenneth-grahame.name: Kenneth Grahame
kenneth-grahame.caution: Two lanes averaged: *The Golden Age* and *Dream Days* are first-person adult reminiscence of childhood; *The Wind in the Willows* is third-person pastoral animal fantasy. A small corpus (~144k) so its lanes are wider than the larger authors'.

e-nesbit.name: E. Nesbit
e-nesbit.caution: The Bastable books are narrated in first person by Oswald, a child pretending not to be the narrator; the fantasy novels use a warm, intrusive third person. These are two distinct lanes and the whole-author numbers average across them.

agatha-christie.name: Agatha Christie
agatha-christie.caution: Two narrators sit inside this corpus: Hastings and the Vicar narrate in first person, while *The Seven Dials Mystery* is third person. Check the per-work table before treating any pronoun or POV number as a single Christie habit.

arthur-conan-doyle.name: Arthur Conan Doyle
arthur-conan-doyle.caution: The full Holmes canon (all US public domain since the 1927 Case-Book predates 1930). Mostly first-person Watson narration, but *A Study in Scarlet* and *The Valley of Fear* each break into a long third-person back-story section, which widens the POV numbers.

g-k-chesterton.name: G. K. Chesterton
g-k-chesterton.caution: Three Father Brown short-story collections — a warm, paradox-driven cozy-mystery voice distinct from Christie's puzzle-plot rhythm. The fetch converter marks no per-story boundaries, so chunk *location* labels are absent; measurement is unaffected.

bram-stoker.name: Bram Stoker
bram-stoker.caution: *Dracula* is epistolary — letters, diaries, telegrams and news clippings across several narrators — which widens every rhythm and POV lane; the other three novels are conventional narration. *The Jewel of Seven Stars* here is the standard Gutenberg edition (PG 3781).

h-g-wells.name: H. G. Wells
h-g-wells.caution: Three of the four novels are first-person retrospective narration; *The Invisible Man* is third person. The scientific romance register also carries more exposition than any other author here.
